transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-05 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood CSM), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Asteria Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Asteria Platform Eng), Sofia Reyes (Asteria PM)

Summary (auto): QBR for Asteria Retail - reviewed September usage spike and cost drivers, investigated two tail-latency incidents during holiday load test, agreed next steps: send detailed cost breakdown, provide SOC2 and security docs, run 2-week dedicated pilot to validate latency & cost, collect eval prompts for quality monitoring.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh it's Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya and Ethan. Maya, Liam, Sofia, you there?
[00:08] Maya: Yeah hi, thanks for doing this. We've got about 45 minutes, hoping to cover the September cost spike and the two incidents we saw during the load tests.
[00:16] Jordan: Yep totally. I'll kick off with a quick usage summary then Priya will go over health, Ethan can take the technical bits.
[00:24] Priya: Quick note - we pulled the cost by route, so we can show which endpoints drove tokens.
[00:30] Ethan: And I'll show the tail-latency traces we captured, there were some KV cache misses and a routing fallback to a higher-cost model in one window.
[00:38] Sofia: A faster run-through of the roadmap items would be great - per-route quotas and the caching improvements we discussed.

[01:05] Jordan: Alright slide one, big picture: month-over-month usage up 38% in September, generation tokens primarily from the product-recs route and chat support route. The spike aligns with your promo week on 9/14. We estimate about 60% of the incremental cost is from longer average response lengths and 20% from retries due to timeouts.
[01:35] Maya: That matches our internal telemetry - we extended context length for recs and didn't cap outputs which ballooned token counts. We should have controlled that.
[01:42] Priya: We annotated the per-route breakdown and highlighted sessions with high avg tokens; we'll send that CSV after.
[01:50] Liam: One question - those retries you mentioned, are they coming from client-side timeouts or service-side throttles?
[01:56] Ethan: Good question. We correlated traces - there were some client retries, but the larger issue was two windows where the smart-routing fell back to a larger model because Dedicated capacity overflowed briefly. That increased cost and latency.
[02:15] Maya: Is that the 9/14 evening window? We saw an order spike then.
[02:19] Ethan: Yep, exact same. Our autoscaling burst didn't kick in fast enough in that region; the fallback policy routed to a hosted variant with higher per-token cost.

[02:55] Sofia: So does Dedicated prevent that fallback if we reserve more capacity? Or is it about tuning autoscale?
[03:02] Jordan: Both. If you up reserved capacity you get predictable throughput and fewer fallbacks, but there's a commit. Ethan can explain short-term mitigations.
[03:09] Ethan: Short term we can tighten the fallback policy so it prefers cheaper model-quantized variants or enable quicker burst capacity. Also prefix/KV caching can cut tokens for common prompts.

[04:10] Maya: We are very sensitive to cost given margins; we need to model Dedicated ROI vs current hosted usage.
[04:17] Priya: We'll include an ROI slide - compare current monthly spend with projected committed pricing under Dedicated plus expected token reduction from caching.

[05:00] Jordan: Next, reliability - two tail-latency incidents flagged at 09:14 and 09:42 during your promo stress test. Ethan, you have the traces?
[05:08] Ethan: Yep. First incident: at 09:14 the KV cache eviction rate spiked due to many distinct session prefixes, so many calls hit the model cold. Tail P99 increased from 280ms to ~1.2s for a short period. Second incident: at 09:42 we saw a routing decision to a model hosted in a different region which added about 250ms network latency plus a heavier model cost.
[05:36] Liam: For the KV cache, any quick wins? We don't have a fancy prefix grouping yet.
[05:41] Ethan: You can reduce entropy in prompts (reduce user-specific tokens), enable shared prefix keys for product recs, and set a slightly larger KV cache TTL on Redwood's side for that route. We can propose a tuned cache profile.
[05:53] Maya: Would adjusting TTL risk stale content? For recs we refresh frequently but could accept a 30s TTL.
[05:59] Ethan: 30s should be fine - depends on your freshness needs.

[06:40] Sofia: Roadmap question - you mentioned per-route quotas. When will that be available?
[06:44] Priya: We're rolling per-route quotas into the next month; beta customers can try it in mid-October. That will help you cap runaway token usage per product route.
[06:52] Jordan: Also, we're releasing improved caching and a quantization recommendation engine that suggests model/quantization per route to save cost.

[08:00] Maya: On security - our security team needs SOC2, KMS integration notes, and proof of data residency.
[08:07] Priya: We'll share SOC2 and ISO certs, and a writeup on KMS/HSM integration. For residency, you can pin region routing and we have Private deployment options if you need on-prem.
[08:21] Liam: For the pilot we'd prefer VPC peering rather than on-prem for speed of setup. Is that supported?
[08:27] Ethan: Yes, we can do VPC peering and a private control plane for the pilot; for the two-week dedicated pilot we recommend VPC peering + reserved nodes so we can mirror your production load.

[09:10] Jordan: Ok let's scope the pilot - primary goals: validate p99 latency under peak load, validate per-token cost with quantization & caching, and measure reliability with routing policies. Timeline suggestion: start week of 10/12 for two weeks.
[09:22] Maya: That works; we'll need to swap contact for infra - Liam will own it.
[09:26] Liam: Yep I'll get access and firewall rules ready. Expect some setup questions.

[10:00] Sofia: A couple feature asks from product: 1) improve structured output consistency for recs, 2) better metrics per model version.
[10:07] Ethan: For structured output we recommend function-calling patterns and temperature profiles; we can run an eval to tune prompts. For per-version metrics we already have model-level dashboards but can add more granularity in the pilot.

[11:12] Maya: Pricing - can you confirm renewal pricing tiers if we pick Dedicated? We have a fiscal decision by 10/20.
[11:19] Jordan: We'll send an illustrative committed pricing sheet. Roughly, Dedicated will look cheaper per-token at your scale but requires a monthly commit. We'll model a few scenarios in the deck.

[12:00] [Ethan shares screen - latency traces]
[12:08] Ethan: Here's the first spike, you can see cache miss pattern, high CPU wait on the node - likely a burst of new prefixes. The blue lines are client retries.
[12:28] Maya: Hmm looks like our client-side retry policy also exacerbated it. We'll tune the client timeouts and exponential backoff.

[14:00] Ethan: Second trace shows cross-region routing. The routing tag switched to us-east-2 clone which has available capacity but higher network RTT. We can tighten region affinity for that route.
[14:15] Liam: Is there any reason routing chose a different region?
[14:18] Ethan: Autoscaler in the primary region was saturated for a short period; fallback policy allowed routing to any compatible region. We can restrict that to only same-region or quantized variants.

[15:40] Priya: Operational items - we'll add a weekly health digest for the next 6 weeks showing per-route tokens, p99 latency, and fallback events.
[15:50] Maya: That would be super helpful.

[16:30] Sofia: On quality regressions, we need eval alerts tied to prompt sets - can Redwood support automated regression detection?
[16:36] Jordan: Yes, our Optimize suite can run evals and alert on regression thresholds. We'll include a sample alert configuration.

[18:05] Maya: One last question on data retention - we need logs for 12 months for audits. Is that on the roadmap?
[18:12] Priya: We have add-on observability retention; 12 months can be provisioned as an enterprise add-on and we'll show pricing.

[19:00] Jordan: Great. Quick recap of next steps - Jordan sends QBR deck + usage/cost CSV; Priya sends SOC2 and KMS notes; Ethan sets up pilot runbook and schedule; Asteria provides eval prompts and infra access details.
[19:18] Maya: Confirming, we'll aim to start pilot week of 10/12 and will make renewal decision by 10/20.

[19:45] Jordan: Anything else?
[19:48] Liam: Just one tiny thing - can we get a list of recommended quantization profiles for the recs model?
[19:54] Ethan: Yes, we'll include a small matrix: float16 for low-latency, 4-bit quant for cost-sensitive routes, and recommendations per route.

[20:30] Sofia: Thanks all, that was productive.
[20:33] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and action items.
[20:37] Maya: Thanks.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels from the recorder may shift, there are occasional filler words and minor ASR errors (e.g., region tag may be transcribed as easttwo).

References/shared artifacts mentioned during call:

End of transcript.
